name: Project Horizon
tagline: Turns third-person sports video into a first-person view from any player you pick.

awards: Backboard.io: Memory Lane: Adaptive AI Journeys
TwelveLabs: Build The Future of Video Understanding with TwelveLabs

problem: Fans see a match from the broadcast camera, never from the perspective of the player making the decisions.
solution: Scene understanding through video models identifies the subject; monocular depth estimation builds a coarse 3D scene and a rough first-person sketch video; an image-to-video diffusion model fine-tuned with LoRA on paired third- and first-person clips renders the final first-person footage on cloud GPUs.
demo_moment: Team-described: pick a player in a soccer clip and watch the play from their eyes.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Took second place overall among 160 submissions and two sponsor prizes.
Fine-tuned a 14B video diffusion model on paired viewpoints during the event, with depth-based priors to keep camera motion plausible.
Seeing a famous player's point of view is an instant hook for any audience.

lessons: Training a model in a weekend is credible when the output is something judges can watch and compare.
